title: Adaptive Prompt Rotation — idea log
body:
Context:
This is a scratchpad for a lightweight feature to rotate prompt templates (and small prompt variants) as part of serving. Idea motivated by two things: 1) reduce brittle signal/overfitting when a single prompt leads to deterministic failure modes (hallucination or repetition), 2) enable low-risk A/B/canary testing of subtle prompt changes without redeploying model weights or changing customer-facing API contract.

Problem statement:
- Some customers see periodic quality regressions tied to certain prompt phrasing (edge-case hallucinations).
- Fixing requires iterative prompt edits + offline evals + rollout, which is slow.
- We want a server-side mechanism to offer multiple prompt templates and rotate them with low overhead and strong telemetry to detect regressions quickly.

Goals:
- Provide an internal feature on the hosted API to attach 2–5 prompt templates to a route (prompt bank).
- Rotation strategies: round-robin, weighted-by-success, adaptive-decay for underperforming variants.
- Collect per-variant telemetry (latency, token cost, success/failure heuristics, quality signals).
- Easy toggle: admin toggle at route level + per-tenant opt-out.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Not a full personalization engine.
- No heavy semantic rewriting or RL-based prompt generation in MVP.

High-level design notes:
- Prompt bank stored as small metadata object attached to route config (JSON array of templates + weights + tags).
- Runtime: pre-render template with user inputs, then call model as usual. Variants share same model key/config.
- Rotation policies handled in router: lightweight (in-memory) selector with sticky affinity option per session id.
- Telemetry: emit variant id per request; add probe hooks to existing eval pipeline to compute simple heuristics (e.g., safety flag count, presence of hallucination markers, length biases).
- Rollout: canary by percentage (e.g., 5% of traffic to variant B) with automatic rollback based on chosen metric thresholds.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to attach three alternative system prompts to a chat route so I can test which phrasing yields fewer hallucinations.
- As an SRE, I want to be able to route only internal test traffic to new prompt variants during rollout.
- As an evaluation engineer, I want telemetry that groups by variant so I can compute quality delta and decide whether to promote.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Route config supports a prompt_bank field with list of strings and optional weights.
- Server emits telemetry: variant_id, prompt_length_tokens, model_response_tokens, latency_ms, safety_flag_count.
- Console UI: small dropdown/pill to show active variants and approximate splits (counts).
- Can rollback variant automatically if safety_flag_count per-1000 > threshold for 10 minutes.

Metrics to track:
- Variant-level: safety_flag_rate, truncation_rate, average_response_length, median latency, token cost per response.
- Business level: %requests affected, %customers with degraded variant, rollback events.
- Statistical: A/B significance via Thompson or bootstrap for small samples.

Experiment plan:
1) Internal-only pilot on non-customer sandbox routes for 1 week. Use 3 variants: baseline, softer-instruction, conservative-answering.
   - N target: ~50k requests across pilot.
2) Compute safety_flag_rate and an n-gram overlap heuristic with ground-truth where available.
3) If conservative variant reduces safety flags by >25% without >15% latency increase or >10% increase in token cost, consider promoting.

Operational considerations / Risks:
- Privacy/leakage: different prompts could change how much user content is echoed. Need to flag if a variant increases direct reflections of user content (possible PII risk).
- Caching: prompt variants reduce cache hit ratio; need to consider prefix caching strategy (cache key must include variant id if prompts affect model input).
- Billing: rotated variants might produce longer outputs; ensure cost metrics are surfaced to customer and internal billing.
- Exploitability: attackers could try to infer or force less-safe variants if rotation policy is predictable. Consider per-session affinity and cryptographic randomness for public routes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Metric definition: what is a conservative, server-side 'safety_flag'? (See existing safety infra; ping Samira and security for a canonical definition.)
- UI: how much surface in Redwood Console? (minimal counters vs. full variant dashboard)
- Sticky sessions: should session-affinity be default? tradeoffs for experimentation clarity vs user experience consistency.
- Persistence: should prompt bank be versioned to allow rollbacks and audit? (probably yes)

Implementation sketch (MVP):
- API: extend route spec: prompt_bank: [{id, template, weight, tags, version}]
- Router: selector middleware that adds X-Prompt-Variant header to request context and persists selection in tracing span.
- Serving runtime: no model changes; just pre-render template. If templates include dynamic helper calls (tools), disallow in MVP.
- Telemetry: log variant_id in regular request row, and emit metric streams to metrics pipeline with dimension variant_id.

Next steps (short horizon):
- Quick spike: implement selector middleware and minimal telemetry tagging; run internal pilot on sandbox route. (Owner: Ishani, Eng lead: Evan)
- Sync with safety team about safety_flag definition and thresholds. (Owner: Ishani)
- Mock Console view: simple per-variant counts + quick rollback button. Product design sketch due in 2 sprints.

Notes to self:
- Keep variant bank small at first (max 5). Avoid combinations of prompt + model variant in MVP (complexity explosion).
- Check implications for Dedicated/Private customers (private control plane might prefer no automatic rotation unless explicitly enabled).

Raw brainstorm snippets (time-stamped):
- 2026-01-18 09:10: "maybe also allow variant tagging for 'safety-tested', 'cheap', 'concise' so policies can prefer certain tags"
- 2026-01-22 14:44: "consider a simple AB-test endpoint param to force variant for debugging"
- 2026-02-02 11:08: "if we wire rotation into the cache key, we should try prefix-KV caching for shared contexts to mitigate hit loss"

END OF SCRATCHPAD
